To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we propose a novel simultaneous feature and dictionary (SFDL)-learning approach for image set based face recognition; (b) our SFDL is able to learn discriminative image set features and dictionaries from raw facial pixels; (c) we propose a deep-SFDL (D- SFDL) method to learn a hierarchy of nonlinear transformations and dictionaries to further improve performance.

we propose a novel SFDL method and a D-SFDL method for image set based face recognition, which can learn discriminative features as well as dictionaries simultaneously from raw pixels, which can be used in a wide range of face recognition applications.

our simultaneous feature and dictionary (SFDL and D) learning method can achieve very competitive or better recognition performance compared to the state-of-the-art methods on five widely used image set-based face data sets, and the proposed method is very efficient in terms of computation time and memory usage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel image set-based face representation and a novel face classification framework.
the development of a new approach to image set based face recognition that is capable of learning discriminative features and class-specific dictionaries simultaneously.

the following three issues: 1) how to learn discriminative image set representations from facial image sets; 2) how to learn hierarchical nonlinear transformations to better exploit the non-linear relationship between face image sets; and 3) how to jointly learn discriminative features (transformations) and dictionaries from facial image sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is very effective in image set-based face recogntion and it is very promising in other image set-based applications.
the proposed SFDL and its D-SFDL extension can achieve very competitive performance in image set based face recognition.

our SFD-L method can learn discriminative features for image sets and our D-SFDL method can learn discriminatively hierarchical nonlinear transformations and dictionaries for image sets, which can significantly improve image set-based face recog- nition performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a SFLD method to jointly learn features and dictionaries from raw face pixels, and further propose a D-SFDL method to jointly learn hierarchical non-linear transformations for face images and class-specific dictionaries.
we propose two novel simultaneous feature and dictionary leaning (SFDL and D- SFDL) methods for face recognition, and show their effectiveness by extensive experiments on five widely used data sets.
our SFDI method achieves the best performance on all the data sets and our D-SFDL method is the second best on all the data set.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed SFDL and deep SFDL methods are very effective in learning discriminative features and dictionary simultaneously, which can significantly improve the performance for image set-based facial image recognition.
the proposed SFDL and its D-SFDL variant can be easily integrated with any image set-based face representation and classification method to boost the performance of image set-based face analysis.
simultaneous learning of feature and dictionary from raw face image pixels is a very powerful tool for image set-based image recognition.
